root_cause.failing_check: packages/blind-client/bootstrap-http.js:137 (this.fetch(...) method invocation) -> the unbound globalThis.fetch fallback at bootstrap-http.js:105 and direct-http.js:132 throws 'TypeError: Failed to execute fetch on Window: Illegal invocation', wrapped as TRANSPORT_FAILURE 'descriptor bootstrap failed' at bootstrap-http.js:170 (the catch-all for non-BlindClientError causes; Peerit-side mirror: relay-consumer.js:1583 passed the same unbound fallback)
root_cause.mechanism: the browser recovery path (app-entry.js -> recoverPeeritSeedWithLimitedCellGetAuthorityV1) passes NO fetch option, so the vendored client's descriptor bootstrap fell back to the UNBOUND globalThis.fetch; native Window.fetch requires the window receiver, and invoked as a method on the client instance it throws Illegal invocation at the very first descriptor request — before any relay request is attempted, which is why the live network trace showed zero failed requests.
root_cause.asymmetry_explained: the live-two-relay Chromium gate passes because it supplies an explicit bound fetch wrapper (tracedFetch); Node callers (publisher, the read-only live verifier) pass because Node's global fetch has no Window receiver requirement; and earlier browser DOM probes passed only because a tracing init-script had wrapped window.fetch with a bound function by accident — the real deployed app, with no wrapper, always failed at the first descriptor fetch.
fix: js/substrate/relay-consumer.js (recovery fetch selection): bind the fallback — options.fetch || globalThis.fetch.bind(globalThis) (options.fetch, when supplied, is used exactly as before)

vendored blind clients (upstream hiverelay codex/blind-client-fetch-binding-20260801 @ 1012ca12): bind the same fallback at packages/blind-client/bootstrap-http.js:105 and packages/blind-client/direct-http.js:132; both browser artifacts rebuilt (control 224158B, cell-get 174037B) and re-vendored with full authority re-verification
root_cause.no_weakening: descriptor signature, chain continuity, hash, epoch-window and admission equality verification are all unchanged; the fix only changes WHO the fetch function's receiver is
